issues.legal_issue: An appellate authority that is not a court cannot condone delay under section 5 of the Limitation Act when the governing special enactment adopts limitation rules only for computing the filing period and gives no express power to extend it.
material_facts: A landholder filed an appeal to the Collector long after the order under appeal and sought condonation under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
The Collector condoned the delay and allowed the appeal; the High Court, on revision, set that order aside.
At the relevant time, section 93 of the special enactment applied limitation provisions only for computation of the filing period.
issues.conclusion: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 did not apply to the appeal before the Collector, and the Collector had no jurisdiction to condone the delay under that section.
issues.legal_principle: The Limitation Act, 1963 applies to proceedings in courts, not ordinarily to proceedings before quasi-judicial tribunals or executive authorities. A special enactment may expressly make section 5 applicable to such proceedings. Section 93, as it then stood, adopted only provisions concerning computation of limitation, found in sections 12 to 24 of the Limitation Act; section 5 concerns extension after computation shows that a filing is late. The Court approved K. Venkaiah v. K. Venkateswara Rao and relied on Town Municipal Council, Athani v. Presiding Officer, Labour Court, Hubli; Nityananda M. Joshi v. Life Insurance Corporation of India; and Sushila Devi v. Ramanandan Prasad.

predicates.special_enactment_appeal_before_non_cour: The proceeding is an appeal under a special enactment before an authority that is not a court.
predicates.limitation_rules_adopted_only_for_comput: The special enactment adopts limitation rules only for computing the filing period.
predicates.no_express_power_to_extend_delay: The governing enactment contains no express provision empowering the authority to extend the filing period upon sufficient cause.

issues.definition: When an appeal under a special enactment is before a non-court authority, the enactment adopts limitation rules only for computation, and it gives no express extension power, the authority cannot condone delay.

issues.legal_issue: A later amendment expressly adding a power to condone delay does not govern an appeal arising under the prior law when the amendment is prospective and the prior text was unambiguous.
material_facts: The appeal arose under section 93 as it stood before its amendment.
A later amendment expressly made section 5 of the Limitation Act applicable to appeals and revisions under the special enactment.
The amendment was prospective, and the Court found that the earlier text was unambiguous and that the amendment was not clarificatory.
issues.conclusion: The later amendment did not assist the appellant; the appeal was governed by section 93 as originally enacted.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the amendment to section 93 by the Andhra Pradesh Tenancy Laws (Amendment) Act, 1979 as a prospective change rather than a clarification of the prior law. Because the earlier text was unambiguous and the amendment was prospective, the amended provision did not govern this appeal.

rule.if: appeal_under_special_enactment and proceeding_arose_under_prior_law and later_amendment_expressly_added_extension_power and later_amendment_was_prospective and prior_text_was_unambiguous

predicates.appeal_under_special_enactment: The proceeding is an appeal under a special enactment.
predicates.proceeding_arose_under_prior_law: The appeal arose under the law as it stood before a later amendment.
predicates.later_amendment_expressly_added_extensio: A later amendment expressly added power to extend the filing period.
predicates.later_amendment_was_prospective: The later amendment was made to operate prospectively.
predicates.prior_text_was_unambiguous: The text governing the proceeding before the amendment was unambiguous.

issues.definition: When an appeal under a special enactment arose under unambiguous prior law and a later prospective amendment expressly adds extension power, that later power does not apply retroactively.
